speaker: Doctor
text: It sounds like you've been through a traumatic event; can you tell me exactly how your leg was positioned when you were first seen after the collision, and is there any numbness or tingling in your foot?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe how your right leg is positioned now compared to your left, and have you noticed any deformity or inability to move it? Additionally, did you experience a "popping" sound at the time of the injury?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Anterior Hip Dislocation (Right)

The leg position you described—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is classic for an anterior hip dislocation, which contradicts the appendicitis diagnosis. I need to confirm this immediately: can you actively lift your right leg straight up off the bed, and is there any numbness on the outer side of your right thigh? REQUEST IMAGERS: Right Hip X-Ray AP and Lateral views.
